(1) Malic acid $\rightarrow$ Oxaloacetic acid
(2) Succinic acid $\rightarrow$ Malic acid
(3) Succinyl-CoA $\rightarrow$ Succinic acid
(4) Isocitrate $\rightarrow$ $\alpha$-ketoglutaric acid
question.html:
Identify the step in tricarboxylic acid cycle, which does not involve oxidation of substrate.
  1. (1)Malic acid → Oxaloacetic acid
  2. (2)Succinic acid → Malic acid
  3. (3)Succinyl-CoA → Succinic acid
  4. (4)Isocitrate → α-ketoglutaric acid
question.stem: Identify the step in tricarboxylic acid cycle, which does not involve oxidation of substrate.

steps: Isocitrate $\rightarrow$ $\alpha$-ketoglutaric acid is an oxidative decarboxylation producing $NADH + H^+$, so it is an oxidation.
Malic acid $\rightarrow$ Oxaloacetic acid is a dehydrogenation producing $NADH + H^+$, so it is an oxidation.
Succinic acid $\rightarrow$ Malic acid (via fumarate) involves the dehydrogenation producing $FADH_2$, so it is an oxidation.
Succinyl-CoA $\rightarrow$ Succinic acid releases CoA and forms $GTP$ (substrate-level phosphorylation) with no electron carrier reduced, so it is not an oxidation: option $3$.
ai_solution.html:
1. Isocitrate → α-ketoglutaric acid is an oxidative decarboxylation producing NADH + H+, so it is an oxidation.
  2. Malic acid → Oxaloacetic acid is a dehydrogenation producing NADH + H+, so it is an oxidation.
  3. Succinic acid → Malic acid (via fumarate) involves the dehydrogenation producing FADH2, so it is an oxidation.
  4. Succinyl-CoA → Succinic acid releases CoA and forms GTP (substrate-level phosphorylation) with no electron carrier reduced, so it is not an oxidation: option 3.
ai_solution.why: Succinyl-CoA to succinic acid is substrate-level phosphorylation (GTP/ATP formed) with no NAD+/FAD reduction; the other three steps produce NADH or FADH2.

question.stem: Which one is the correct product of DNA dependent RNA polymerase to the given template? 3’TACATGGCAAATATCCATTCA5’

steps: DNA-dependent RNA polymerase synthesises RNA complementary and antiparallel to the template strand, reading $3'\to5'$ and building $5'\to3'$, using U instead of T.

Option 4 contains T (DNA), option 2 has AAAG in place of CCG, option 3 has GGG in place of GGU; only option $1$ matches exactly.
ai_solution.html:
1. DNA-dependent RNA polymerase synthesises RNA complementary and antiparallel to the template strand, reading 3'→5' and building 5'→3', using U instead of T.
  2. Complementing 3'-TACATGGCAAATATCCATTCA-5' base by base gives 5'-AUGUACCGUUUAUAGGUAAGU-3'.
  3. Option 4 contains T (DNA), option 2 has AAAG in place of CCG, option 3 has GGG in place of GGU; only option 1 matches exactly.
ai_solution.why: RNA is complementary and antiparallel to the 3'->5' template with U in place of T: 5'AUGUACCGUUUAUAGGUAAGU3'.

question.stem: As per ABO blood grouping system, the blood group of father is $\mathrm{B^{+}}$, mother is $\mathrm{A^{+}}$ and child is $\mathrm{O^{+}}$. Their respective genotype can be Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

statements.label: A
statements.text: $\mathrm{I^{B}i/I^{A}i/ii}$

statements.label: B
statements.text: $\mathrm{I^{B}I^{B}/I^{A}I^{A}/ii}$

statements.label: C
statements.text: $\mathrm{I^{A}I^{B}/iI^{A}/I^{B}i}$

statements.label: D
statements.text: $\mathrm{I^{A}i/I^{B}i/I^{A}i}$

statements.label: E
statements.text: $\mathrm{iI^{B}/iI^{A}/I^{A}I^{B}}$

steps: Blood group O is only possible with genotype $ii$, so the child is $ii$ and got one $i$ allele from each parent.
So the father (group B) must be $I^{B}i$ and the mother (group A) must be $I^{A}i$.
Statement A ($I^{B}i/I^{A}i/ii$) matches. B fails because homozygous parents cannot have an $ii$ child, and C, D and E give the wrong phenotypes.
Only A is correct, which is option $1$.
ai_solution.html:
1. Blood group O is only possible with genotype ii, so the child is ii and got one i allele from each parent.
  2. So the father (group B) must be IBi and the mother (group A) must be IAi.
  3. Statement A (IBi/IAi/ii) matches. B fails because homozygous parents cannot have an ii child, and C, D and E give the wrong phenotypes.
  4. Only A is correct, which is option 1.
ai_solution.why: An O child (ii) needs an i allele from each parent, so the B father must be I^Bi and the A mother I^Ai; only A fits.

step_list: Match each statement's genotype triple, in father/mother/child order, to phenotypes B, A, O (C, D and E fail at once: wrong phenotype in the father, mother or child slot)
Of the remaining A and B, apply that an O (ii) child needs an i allele from each parent, so homozygous I^B I^B x I^A I^A cannot give ii
difficulty.why: Medium: two short steps of Mendelian recall, with options 3 and 4 eliminated by a slot-order glance, but one real rival remains -- B only is what a candidate gets by checking phenotypes alone, and only the ii-child-needs-heterozygous-parents step separates it from A only.
difficulty.what_makes_it_hard: Statement B is phenotypically correct for all three people, so a candidate who checks only phenotypes and forgets the child must receive i from both parents is drawn to option 2.

steps: Exophthalmic goiter (Graves' disease) is hypersecretion of thyroid hormone with protruding eyeballs: $A \to III$.
Acromegaly results from excessive secretion of growth hormone in adults: $B \to IV$.
Cushing's syndrome results from excess cortisol, giving moon face and hyperglycemia: $C \to I$.
Cretinism results from hyposecretion of thyroid hormone, with stunted growth: $D \to II$.
$A\text{-}III, B\text{-}IV, C\text{-}I, D\text{-}II$ matches option $4$.
ai_solution.html:
1. Exophthalmic goiter (Graves' disease) is hypersecretion of thyroid hormone with protruding eyeballs: A → III.
  2. Acromegaly results from excessive secretion of growth hormone in adults: B → IV.
  3. Cushing's syndrome results from excess cortisol, giving moon face and hyperglycemia: C → I.
  4. Cretinism results from hyposecretion of thyroid hormone, with stunted growth: D → II.
  5. A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II matches option 4.
ai_solution.why: Exophthalmic goiter = thyroid hypersecretion with protruding eyes (III); acromegaly = excess GH (IV); Cushing's = excess cortisol, moon face (I); cretinism = thyroid hyposecretion, stunted growth (II).
